inputs.modified_text: John Mahama’s commitment to the rule of law is meaningful only if the law protects people with the least power—not just those whose views dominate a “collective agreement.” Culture and consensus are shaped by inequality, so they cannot be treated as neutral reasons to deny vulnerable people their rights.
